extracted.intended_audience: public health communicators, program planners, and health education professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, developing, pretesting, implementing, and evaluating health communication programs, including stages, planning steps, message/materials development and pretesting methods, and applicable theories and frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1: Planning and Strategy Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall stage focused on planning and strategy development for health communication programs (Stage 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 1. Assess the Health Issue/Problem and Identify All Components of a Solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning step: assess the health issue/problem and identify all components of a solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the first planning step under Planning Steps (Stage 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2. Define Communication Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning step: define clear communication objectives for the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the second planning step under Planning Steps (Stage 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 3. Define and Learn About Intended Audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning step: define the intended audiences and learn about them to inform communication strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the third planning step under Planning Steps (Stage 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 4. Explore Settings, Channels, and Activities to Reach Intended Audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning step: explore appropriate settings, communication channels, and activities to reach intended audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the fourth planning step under Planning Steps (Stage 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 5. Identify Potential Partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning step: identify potential partners to support program development and implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the fifth planning step under Planning Steps (Stage 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6. Develop a Communication Strategy; Draft Communication and Evaluation Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning step: develop an overarching communication strategy and draft both communication and evaluation plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as the sixth planning step under Planning Steps (Stage 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2: Developing and Pretesting Concepts, Messages, and Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall stage focused on developing and pretesting message concepts and communication materials (Stage 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Steps in Developing and Pretesting Messages and Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Overarching set of steps guiding the development and pretesting process for messages and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: 1. Review Existing Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Step: review existing materials as part of developing and pretesting messages and materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the enumerated Steps in Developing and Pretesting Messages and Materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2. Develop and Test Message Concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Step: develop message concepts and test them (e.g., concept testing) before producing final materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the enumerated Steps in Developing and Pretesting Messages and Materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3. Decide What Materials to Develop
rubrics_metrics.description: Step: decide which types of materials are needed (formats, lengths, channels) based on objectives and audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the enumerated Steps in Developing and Pretesting Messages and Materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4. Develop Messages and Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Step: create the actual messages and materials (copy, design, media) for the communication program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the enumerated Steps in Developing and Pretesting Messages and Materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: 5. Pretest Messages and Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Step: pretest draft messages and materials with intended audiences to assess comprehension, appeal, and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pretesting is listed as an explicit step; related subsections include theater tests, questionnaires, scripts, and sample tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 3: Implementing the Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall stage focused on program implementation (Stage 3), including preparing to implement, maintaining partnerships, media relations, and monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 4: Assessing Effectiveness and Making Refinements
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall stage focused on outcome evaluation, assessing effectiveness, refining the program, and revising the evaluation plan (Stage 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Communication Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance indicates multiple types of communication research (quantitative, quasi-quantitative, qualitative) are relevant to program development, pretesting, and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section headings point to using different research methods depending on the question (surveys, focus groups, intercepts, diaries, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative Research Methods: Surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Use surveys as a quantitative method for measuring audience characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, and responses to materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Quantitative Research Methods and as a pretesting/evaluation tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-Quantitative Research Methods: Pretesting Messages and Materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quasi-quantitative approaches (e.g., theater-style testing, commercial ad rating interpretation) for pretesting messages and materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes theater-style tests, sample pretest questionnaires, and interpreting average ratings for ads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative Research Methods: Focus Groups and In-Depth Interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Use qualitative methods like focus groups and in-depth interviews to explore audience reactions, meanings, and message refinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section headings include About Focus Groups and About In-Depth Interviews; sample moderator guides and screener forms are referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central-Location Intercept Interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: A quasi-quantitative/intercept method for collecting immediate reactions from target audiences at central locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among pretesting/intercept research methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diaries and Activity Logs
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualitative/quasi-qualitative method for collecting longitudinal self-reported data about behaviors and contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a pretesting/qualitative method option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theater-Style Tests and Sample Theater-Style Pretest Questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: Use theater-style testing (showing rough cuts or ads to groups) with structured questionnaires and scripts to assess responses to audiovisual materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes sample scripts and questionnaires for hosting theater-style tests; used for pretesting video/commercial-style materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producing Rough-Cut Video for Pretesting/Theater Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance to produce rough-cut video materials for use in pretesting (theater-style tests) to get audience feedback before final production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a subtopic under pretesting audiovisual materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample Tools and Forms (e.g., Focus Group Screener, Intercept Questionnaire, Moderator's Guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide and use sample forms and instruments (focus group screener, intercept questionnaire, moderator's guide) to standardize research and pretesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple sample forms and templates are referenced under Stage 2 and appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gatekeeper Reviews and Readability Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct gatekeeper reviews (review by stakeholders/decision-makers) and readability testing to ensure materials are appropriate and accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among communication research and pretesting activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Theories, Models, and Constructs (Individual, Interpersonal, Organizational/Community/Societal Levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply social science theories, planning frameworks, and models (e.g., Health Belief Model, Social Cognitive Theory, Stages of Change, Community Organization Theory, Diffusion of Innovations, Organizational Change Theory) at appropriate levels (individual, interpersonal, organization/community/societal) to guide strategy and message design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section lists Selected Social Science Theories, Models, and Constructs and groups them by level (Individual Level, Interpersonal Level, Organization/Community/Societal Level).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Theoretical Frameworks: Social Cognitive Theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider Social Cognitive Theory as a guide for designing messages that target behavioral determinants such as self-efficacy and observational learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Interpersonal/Individual level theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Theoretical Frameworks: Health Belief Model
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the Health Belief Model for addressing perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, and barriers in message design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among Individual Level theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Theoretical Frameworks: Stages of Change
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Stages of Change model to tailor messages to individuals' readiness for behavior change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Individual Level theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Theoretical Frameworks: Consumer Information Processing Model and Behavioral Intentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use models like the Consumer Information Processing Model and constructs like Behavioral Intentions to inform message processing and persuasive strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Individual Level or related theory sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Theoretical Frameworks: Community Organization Theory and Organizational Change Theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Community Organization Theory and Organizational Change Theory to inform interventions at organizational and community levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Organization/Community/Societal Level theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Theoretical Frameworks: Diffusion of Innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Diffusion of Innovations theory to plan how new behaviors or messages spread through populations and networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Organization/Community/Societal Level theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Planning Frameworks: Social Marketing and PRECEDE-PROCEED
rubrics_metrics.description: Use program planning frameworks such as Social Marketing and PRECEDE-PROCEED to structure strategy, planning, and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the Planning Frameworks, Theories, and Models of Change appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage/Appendix Use: Communication Program Plan, Strategy Statement/Creative Brief, Evaluation Plan, Partnership Plan, Sample Promotion Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard planning documents and templates (communication program plan, creative brief, evaluation plan, partnership plan, promotion plan) to organize program activities and documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple sample forms and templates are referenced as part of Stage 1 and Stage 2 appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretesting Data Tabulation and Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tabulate responses to closed- and open-ended questions and interpret average ratings (e.g., for commercial ads) to inform material revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections reference tabulating responses and using average ratings to interpret standard pretesting questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining Media Relations and Working With the Media During a Crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance sections address maintaining media relations after launch and working with media in crisis situations as part of implementation and communications management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Stage 3 topics related to implementation and media relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why Outcome Evaluation Is Important / Conducting Outcome Evaluation / Revising the Outcome Evaluation Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria emphasizing the importance of outcome evaluation and guidance on conducting and revising outcome/evaluation plans to assess program impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Stage 4 subtopics; underscores iterative evaluation and plan refinement.
